record.paper_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
record.original_question: Can the relevant boundary conditions for the free fermion and for the super-Virasoro minimal model SVIR3 be derived directly from first principles, or alternatively by adapting the methods of Novak and Runkel?

evidence.quote: It would be interesting to derive the boundary conditions for the free fermion and SVIR3 from first principles or using the methods of Novak and Runkel [84].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider two-dimensional conformal field theories defined on surfaces with boundary. Two specific fermionic/superconformal theories of interest are:

(i) the free Majorana fermion CFT (central charge c = 1/2), and

(ii) the third unitary N = 1 super-Virasoro minimal model SVIR3, i.e. the unitary superconformal minimal model with central charge c = c(m) for m = 5 in the family
   c(m) = 3/2 · (1 − 8/(m(m+2))),
which is the supersymmetric analogue of a unitary Virasoro minimal model and contains fields organised under the N = 1 super-Virasoro algebra.

For each of these theories, conformal (and, where relevant, superconformal-preserving) boundary conditions can be specified by boundary states |B⟩ in the closed-string Hilbert space satisfying gluing conditions of Cardy/Ishibashi type, together with an integrality (Cardy) condition on the open-string spectrum.

Problem. Derive the complete set of (elementary) conformal boundary conditions, together with their boundary states and the corresponding annulus/open-string partition functions, for the free Majorana fermion and for the super-Virasoro minimal model SVIR3, by either:

(a) a direct first-principles construction (for example, solving the Cardy/Ishibashi gluing and integrality conditions intrinsically in the fermionic/superconformal category of representations), or

(b) an adaptation of the classifying-algebra and TFT-with-defects methodology used to construct boundary conditions for bosonic rational CFTs from a modular tensor category and a special symmetric Frobenius algebra, suitably extended to the fermionic/super setting.

Produce in either approach an explicit list of boundary states, verify the Cardy condition, and exhibit the boundary structure constants.
artifact.category_tag: Boundary conditions in superconformal field theory
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work by Runkel and collaborators (notably "Fermionic CFTs and classifying algebras", JHEP 06 (2020) 025) develops fermionic classifying algebras for boundaries, defects and interfaces and applies the framework to the fermionic Ising model (free Majorana fermion) and the fermionic tri-critical Ising model (first unitary N=1 super-minimal model). This addresses the methodology for the free fermion and lower super-minimal models, but a complete first-principles or classifying-algebra derivation specifically for SVIR3 does not appear to be explicitly carried out in the literature found. The problem therefore appears partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Fermionic CFTs and classifying algebras
status_evidence.snippet: Defines fermionic classifying algebras for boundaries, defects and interfaces; applies the framework to the fermionic Ising model and the fermionic tri-critical Ising model (first unitary N=1 super-minimal model).
status_evidence.claim: The Novak–Runkel-style methodology has been extended to fermionic CFTs, providing boundary conditions for the free fermion and the simplest super-Virasoro minimal model.

status_evidence.title: Defects in the tri-critical Ising model
status_evidence.snippet: Studies defects (and via folding, boundaries) in the tri-critical Ising model, the first unitary N=1 superconformal minimal model.
status_evidence.claim: Earlier work treats boundaries/defects in the simplest super-Virasoro minimal model but not directly the higher SVIR3.
